{{Short description|French mathematician}}
{{for|the neo-Impressionist painter|Pierre Emile Lelong}}
[[Image:Pierre Lelong.jpg|thumb|right|Lelong in 1967]]
'''Pierre Lelong'''  (14 March 1912 Paris – 12 October 2011)<ref name="academy">[http://www.academie-sciences.fr/academie/membre/Lelong_Pierre.htm Pierre Lelong] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810003403/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/academie/membre/Lelong_Pierre.htm |date=2011-08-10 }} at the académie des sciences</ref> was a French mathematician who introduced the [[Poincaré–Lelong equation]], the [[Lelong number]] and the concept of [[plurisubharmonic function]]s.

==Career==
Lelong earned his doctorate in 1941 from the [[École Normale Supérieure]], under the supervision of [[Paul Montel]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=24207}}</ref> On 5 June 1981 Lelong received an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] from the Faculty of 
Mathematics and Science at [[Uppsala University]], [[Sweden]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/|title = Honorary doctorates - Uppsala University, Sweden| date=9 June 2023 }}</ref>
He became a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1985.<ref name="academy"/>

{{blockquote|Lelong has made many pioneering contributions in mathematics. Especially of great impact is his work on the Poincaré-Lelong equation, closed [[positive current]]s and Lelong numbers. The best way to understand this very important part of his work is to look at it from the historic perspective of constructing meromorphic functions on abstractly defined complex manifolds and see how his contributions fit in a pivotal way into the global landscape in the theory of [[several complex variables]].<br>The theory of several complex variables studies complex-analytic objects such as holomorphic and meromorphic functions and maps, complex-analytic subvarieties, holomorphic vector bundles, and coherent analytic sheaves. When a complex-analytic manifold or space is projective algebraic, by definition it is embedded inside a complex projective space and there are many complex- analytic objects on it which are constructed from those on the complex projective space. When a complex-analytic manifold is abstractly defined by piecing together local holomorphic charts, the construction of complex-analytic objects on it is a problem of fundamental importance.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Skoda, Henri|author2=Demailly, Jean-Pierre|author3=Siu, Yum-Tong|title=In Memory of Pierre Lelong|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=61|issue=6|year=2014|pages=586–596|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201406/rnoti-p586.pdf?adat=June/July%202014&trk=201406586&cat=feature&galt=feature|doi=10.1090/noti1137|doi-access=free}} (quote from Siu, p. 589)</ref>}}

==Personal life==
He married another mathematician, [[Jacqueline Ferrand]], in 1947; they separated in 1977.<ref>{{citation|title=Women mathematicians in France in the mid-twentieth century|first=Yvette|last=Kosmann-Schwarzbach|doi=10.1080/17498430.2014.976804|journal=BSHM Bulletin: Journal of the British Society for the History of Mathematics|year=2015|volume=30|issue=3|pages=227–242|arxiv=1502.07597|s2cid=119148294}}.</ref>
